claim_boundary: This artifact is a preregistered classification corpus. Mitigation and detection counts require baseline reproduction, patched controls, exact compiler/runtime coverage, and raw run evidence.

boundaries: destructor side effects can occur before the second allocator call
arbitrary untracked pointers can reach conventional raw behavior
a stale free after legitimate same-address reuse can target the new allocation
this is retained-ownership detection rather than general UAF prevention
allocator_visible_double_free.claim: Tracked cache, quarantine, tag, or lifecycle ownership can fail-stop a second allocator-visible reclaim during its recorded ownership window.
required_conditions: the first reclaim publishes a tracked ownership or lifecycle record
the second reclaim reaches a UniAlloc entry point before legitimate backend reuse
the fail-stop occurs before duplicate cache or quarantine ownership is published

boundaries: a later invalid reclaim may independently encounter allocator lifecycle checks
a schedule change is not evidence of mitigation without the original race witness and mechanism-specific oracle
concurrency_unsoundness.claim: Type Isolation does not enforce Send, Sync, aliasing, or synchronization invariants during ordinary memory access.
required_conditions: the race witness reproduces under a matched allocator configuration
allocator substitution does not change the synchronization schedule contract

boundaries: a nested Rust heap allocation may still pass through UniAlloc and must be analyzed separately
allocator substitution can change symptoms without covering the vulnerable object lifecycle
foreign_allocator_boundary.claim: Objects privately managed by arenas, mmap regions, custom allocators, or foreign allocators do not receive per-object Type Isolation from an outer allocation identity.
required_conditions: the experiment records the allocator that owns the failing object
compiler and runtime audits distinguish outer allocation coverage from inner object coverage

boundaries: guard pages are a separate policy for eligible page-scale boundary crossings
sub-page, intra-object, and fixed-heap overflows remain outside guard-page coverage
heap_oob.claim: Type Isolation does not validate ordinary loads or stores and therefore does not stop the out-of-bounds access.
required_conditions: the baseline OOB witness reproduces
the Type Isolation arm preserves the same critical-site coverage as typed_plain

boundaries: UniAlloc does not implement general pointer provenance
unknown deallocation metadata is accepted on selected recovery paths
external C allocator ownership remains outside the instrumented path
invalid_deallocation.claim: Known tracked addresses can reject mismatched layout, identity, or ownership at allocator reclaim boundaries.
required_conditions: the invalid free reaches UniAlloc rather than a foreign allocator
an exact recovery, tag, cache-ownership, or lifecycle record exists
the oracle identifies an allocator-specific fail-stop before raw release

boundaries: an eventual invalid deallocation may independently encounter a tracked lifecycle check
a changed address or schedule is not evidence of language-invariant enforcement
language_invariant_violation.claim: Allocator identity does not enforce Rust aliasing, pinning, alignment, or language-level dynamic type invariants during access.
required_conditions: the original provenance, aliasing, pinning, or alignment witness reproduces
the allocator arms use matched compiler and optimization settings

boundaries: panic-abort builds do not exercise unwind-triggered double drop
user Drop code can perform unsafe side effects before allocator detection
the registry window is finite and a later legitimate reuse changes the address epoch
panic_double_drop.claim: A duplicated deallocation reached during unwind can fail-stop when the first deallocation remains represented in allocator lifecycle state.
required_conditions: the PoC runs with unwind semantics and reproduces the duplicate deallocation
both deallocations reach UniAlloc
the first deallocation remains in a tracked cache, quarantine, tag, or lifecycle state

boundaries: same-identity reuse remains allowed
a stale dereference before reuse remains observable
fallback, custom-allocator, and foreign-allocator paths receive no Type Isolation guarantee
a changed address-reuse outcome leaves the source vulnerability present
reuse_dependent_uaf.claim: A derived same-layout A-to-B grooming experiment can test whether exact-identity cache routing removes a cross-identity reuse edge; the published advisory witness remains a no-direct-effect control.
required_conditions: the published vulnerable behavior reproduces under both typed_plain and typeiso
a separately hashed derived grooming witness reproduces under typed_plain
the derived witness requires reuse by a distinct exact identity
the allocation, reclaim, and replacement sites carry exact nonzero compiler metadata
the object is eligible for and participates in the semantic type cache
critical-site fallback and recovery mismatch counts are zero

boundaries: allocator-side software tags do not validate ordinary loads or stores
same-identity cache reuse is an intentional part of the exact-identity contract
scheduler or address changes without a mechanism-specific oracle are inconclusive
same_identity_or_pre_reuse_uaf.claim: Type Isolation cannot invalidate a stale pointer before reuse or distinguish it after legitimate same-identity reuse.
required_conditions: the baseline stale-access witness reproduces
the original trigger does not require a distinct-identity cache reuse edge
the comparison keeps optional delayed-free policy separate

boundaries: force initialization is a separate policy and only helps allocation-backed byte regions that zeroing makes safe
same-identity stale bytes, stack storage, and foreign buffers remain outside that policy
zero bytes do not form a valid value for every Rust type
uninitialized_exposure.claim: Type Isolation does not track initializedness and therefore does not detect the invalid read.
required_conditions: the baseline uninitialized-byte or invalid-value witness reproduces
the Type Isolation comparison does not enable force initialization

cohorts.rudra_poc: 19 RustSec cases present in Rudra-PoC, including 18 source reproducers and one explicit no-PoC stub
cohorts.rustsec_extended: 21 additional advisories selected for temporal, allocator-boundary, spatial, and provenance coverage

exclusion: pure panic or denial of service without a memory-safety primitive
stack-only memory corruption outside the predeclared provenance and access-time control stratum
cryptographic or logic defects without heap memory safety
duplicate advisory aliases for the same package and root cause
inclusion: public RustSec advisory with a direct heap memory-safety primitive, or a predeclared mechanism-boundary negative control
heap allocation, access, or reclaim participates in the main failure chain for derived reuse experiments or boundary candidates
one of the preregistered temporal, reclaim, spatial, initialization, concurrency, or provenance strata
advisory date is no later than the corpus snapshot date
selection_protocol.prevalence_use: This subset cannot estimate Rust ecosystem prevalence or the percentage of RustSec vulnerabilities mitigated.
selection_protocol.sampling_frame: RustSec advisories at the pinned commit, with Rudra-PoC as a reproducibility stratum rather than the universe
